The Goursat subspace correspondence gives exactly [a r]_q[b s]_q[r k]_q[s k]_q |GL_k(q)| distinct X with dimension r+s-k. Thus multiplication of independent counts gives the formula with correct ideal dimensions. Characteristic two is valid because the bracket is alternating. The standalone verifier exhaustively checks every subspace for dimensions 3,5,8 over prime fields; results match. Finite tests do not prove the infinite generality, which follows from the explicit bijections.

value.rationale: The motivating literature identifies only selected graph-ideals of the concrete complete-bipartite Lie algebras, leaving the full ideal lattice unexplained. The theorem gives a natural, complete dimension-by-dimension ideal invariant uniformly for arbitrarily large two-parameter graph families and every finite field, not a fixed computational slice. Goursat links, arbitrary center subspaces and graph lifts contribute essential noncoordinate strata, making the distinction from graph-ideals mathematically substantive; the case (a,b)=(2,2) already has 247 ideals over F2. This is a useful closed input for finite-field ideal zeta and related representation-count studies, though no unproved downstream result is asserted.
